values.note: Sixteen RV sites with electricity; the other fourteen of the campground's thirty are tent sites.

sites.source: https://www.mycountyparks.com/county/Decatur/Park/Little-River-Recreation-Area ('Thirty campsites are located on the area. Of these, sixteen are RV sites with electricity, and fourteen are tent sites'), read 2026-11-02

facilities.source: https://www.mycountyparks.com/county/Decatur/Park/Little-River-Recreation-Area ('Potable water is within close proximity to all sites and a shower house with modern restrooms is located in the campground'), read 2026-11-02

values.note: Self-serve registration kiosk; cash or check only, no cards. Cabins and shelters book online; campsites do not.

booking.source: https://www.mycountyparks.com/county/Decatur/Park/Little-River-Recreation-Area ('We do not accept camping reservations. The campground is all first-come first-served. There is a self-serve registration kiosk ... cash or check. Credit or debit cards are not accepted at this time'), read 2026-11-02

values.note: Decatur County: electric $20 a night, non-electric $15 (the non-electric sites are the tent sites).

fees.source: https://www.mycountyparks.com/county/Decatur/Park/Little-River-Recreation-Area ('Camping rates at Little River are $15 for a non-electric site and $20 for an electric camping site'), read 2026-11-02

note: Decatur County Conservation Board campground, managed jointly with Iowa DNR, on a peninsula in 787-acre Little River Lake, within the 2,200-acre recreation area. Two campground docks, and boats may be pulled up on shore. Jet skis and ski boats are prohibited on the lake. Three rental cabins are separate. --Claude
summary: Decatur County page confirms FCFS, $20 electric ($15 non-electric, tent sites), showers, potable water. Sites count 30->16 RV (14 are tent). Note corrected: the 2,200 acres is the recreation area, the lake is 787 acres. Page gives no amperage or campground season. Pin good; lakefront holds on imagery.
flags: WATERFRONT holds at lakefront: imagery at the pin shows RV pads (two rigs parked) on the outer south side of the peninsula loop, about 50 m of open grass with scattered trees and a campground dock to Little River Lake, no road or day use in between. Pads on the inner side of the loop are behind the loop road. Pin is on the pads (good).
